subject: Data locality verification & cross-region activation request
messages:
From: Maria Dias <maria.dias@acme-financial.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@acme-financial.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Data locality verification & cross-region activation request

Hi Sofia / Lauren,

We’re preparing the evidence pack for Acme’s upcoming audit and need a clear, written confirmation of how Redwood will behave for our Private deployment in the event of an EU outage that triggers APAC activation. Specifically we need:

- A high-level network diagram showing where customer data (requests, logs, and artifacts) will traverse during normal ops and after activation.
- The activation criteria (what triggers a regional failover) and any automatic vs manual steps.
- Confirmation on where keys and plaintext live during failover (KMS/CMEK residency).
- A short test plan showing how Redwood will prove during a tabletop that no EU-personal-data is exposed unintentionally when APAC takes traffic.

Attached is a short questionnaire the auditors gave us (acme-req-questions.pdf). Can you respond with these artifacts or point us to the relevant runbook? We ideally need a preliminary response by COB Wed 24 Jun to feed into the audit timeline.

Thanks,

Maria Dias
Security Assurance Lead
Acme Financial
[Attachment: acme-req-questions.pdf]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>
To: Maria Dias <maria.dias@acme-financial.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data locality verification & cross-region activation request

Hi Maria,

Thank you — we reviewed your questionnaire and have prepared the initial artifacts you requested. High-level answers here, and I’ve attached a network diagram and our activation test plan for review. Full runbook and evidence templates are in the Drive link I’ll share after your quick confirmation below.

Summary answers (short):
- Architecture: Your Private deployment will be anchored to EU primary hosts inside your VPC peering arrangement. APAC will be configured as a warm standby in a separate VPC (customer-owned) that accepts traffic only when activation rules are met.
- Data flows during failover: Only encrypted application payloads and metadata are forwarded to APAC. All cryptographic keys (customer CMKs) remain in the EU KMS; APAC nodes perform envelope decryption using short-lived keys wrapped by the EU CMK — plaintext is only processed in the region where the key is unwrapped.
- Activation criteria: failover is triggered when (a) control-plane health checks across EU podset fall below the configured SLO for >5 minutes AND (b) automated routing fallback cannot restore within the configured window OR customer triggers manual activation. We capture precise timestamps and use an immutable audit log for the event.
- Logs & telemetry: Application logs that contain PII are redacted before any cross-region replication; operational metrics (aggregated) are allowed for continuity but are labeled/filtered to avoid account-level PII leakage.

Attached artifacts: sofia-netdiag-v1.png (network diagram) and activation-test-plan.xlsx (test matrices + acceptance criteria).

Open questions for Acme that affect evidence:
1) Can Acme provide the allowed egress port range (we assume 443 + 8443 for control-plane and metrics) and any firewall restrictions for the APAC VPC?
2) Target RTO you want Redwood to guarantee for this warm-standby arrangement? We typically design for an RTO of 15–30 minutes in warm-standby, with a 5-minute detection window.
3) Any specific key management constraints from your KMS audit team? (e.g., no external KMS calls from APAC nodes).

Next steps we propose: 30-minute call with your security and network ops, plus Equinox (partner) to validate peering and route propagation. If that works, Marcus will own the tabletop test schedule and Karthik will provide the final runbook redaction for audit.

Action items (for Redwood):
- Share Drive link to full runbook and historical activation playbooks (Sofia) — once you confirm the egress ports.
- Prepare redaction report for logs and an S3 snapshot procedure for auditors (Marcus).
- Schedule tabletop (Karthik).

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sofia-netdiag-v1.png]
[Attachment: activation-test-plan.xlsx]

From: Maria Dias <maria.dias@acme-financial.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>, partner@equinox.io
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 12:41:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data locality verification & cross-region activation request

Thanks Sofia — that’s helpful. A few clarifying items before we loop in auditors: 

- On KMS: our compliance team requires that CMKs never be exported or used outside the EU. Your envelope flow sounds promising but we need explicit confirmation that APAC hosts never have access to plaintext keys and that all unwrap operations are gatekept by an EU-only HSM/KMS.
- On logs: can you provide an example redaction rule for error traces that might include customer identifiers? We need to show auditors concrete redaction patterns.
- On routing: will DNS failover cause any cache-expiry issues with client-side timeouts? Can you list the expected client-side TTLs we should communicate to our app teams?

We’ll also want Equinox to confirm the peering behaviour (partner@equinox.io is CC’d). If you can provide the Drive link and a proposed 30-minute slot for Wednesday 24 Jun morning CET, I’ll try to book.

Regards,

Maria

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data locality verification & cross-region activation request

Hi Maria — quick technical confirmations below to address your auditors’ likely follow-ups.

- KMS handling: Confirmed. Customer CMKs remain exclusively in the EU KMS/HSM. APAC hosts never hold unwrapped CMKs. We use envelope encryption: APAC nodes receive only ciphertext; unwrap requests must be proxied through the EU control plane which applies customer KMS policies. If policy forbids any cross-region calls, we can enable a manual-key-unlock process that requires customer approval (documented in the runbook).

- Log redaction example (we’ll attach templates in Drive):
  * Error trace rule: strip or hash any field matching regex for account_id, email, ssn patterns. Keep only non-identifying error codes and timestamps.
  * Audit snapshot flow: for auditor snapshots we provide a redacted S3 export plus a separate assurance checklist showing the regex rules applied.

- DNS and client TTLs: Recommended client-facing TTLs: 60s for edge DNS used in client SDKs, 300s for internal service discovery. We’ll include a short note for app teams about retry/backoff windows to avoid split-brain during propagation.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Sofia will share the Drive runbook link once Acme confirms egress ports.
2) We provision a short tabletop test (non-production traffic) scheduled Wed 24 Jun 09:00–09:30 CET.
3) Post-tabletop we will create a redaction report and provide the auditor snapshot (redacted) plus the immutable activation audit log.

HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.example.com/contacts/ACME-32145 (we’ll attach artifacts there).

Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attached: activation-test-plan.xlsx - final will be pushed to Drive]
